title: Supply adapter port family + sandbox mocks (Constitution V, PRD 9.3)
body:
Feature-sized — route through Spec Kit.

Create the supplier-agnostic port family for the P0 bookable component map: hotels (bedbank net rates), activities/tickets, transfers, car rental — each with search, quote-with-markup, book, cancel — plus deterministic sandbox mock implementations for tests. Design the port contracts for the PRD 9.2/9.4 engineering realities: quote-then-book with price hold/expiry + re-quote, multi-currency, partial-failure handling in multi-supplier carts, and a merchant-of-record field per component. No supplier API shapes may leak outside an adapter. Caching split per INV-025/026: static supplier content (descriptions, amenities, media refs) is materialized into Postgres derived tables with semantic keys; live rates/quotes are NEVER cached beyond their hold/expiry. Real aggregator integrations (RateHawk/Viator/Mozio/CarTrawler class) come later behind the same ports.

title: Budget allocator + quote-then-book flow (PRD 9.1/9.2/9.4) via SDD
body:
Feature-sized — route through Spec Kit. The core AI differentiator per Constitution III.

Budget allocator: split a total budget (hard cap or target) across categories (flights/transport 35-45%, accommodation 30-40%, activities 10-15%, local transport/transfers 5-10%, buffer 5-10% — tunable by trip type), pull live options per category via the supply ports, assemble to fit, re-balance when a category runs over. In P0 the flights/transport category is allocated as a reserve/manual estimate only — there is no live flight lookup (no flights supply port; deep-link flights are P2 per INV-022), so treat it as the budget anchor, not a profit line. Output: itinerary (canonical schema) with visible per-category and per-day budget breakdown.

Quote-then-book: price holds with expiry, re-quote on expiry, transparent currency conversion, multi-supplier cart with partial-failure handling (one component fails, others hold).

AI wiring (INV-013): planner drafting through LLMPort via the official Anthropic SDK, ALL calls on claude-haiku-4-5 (no Opus — operator decision). Claude tools defined in code under packages/llm/src/tools/ as typed zod definitions (betaZodTool), one file per tool, wrapping the supply ports: search_hotel_rates, search_activities, quote_transfer, quote_car_rental. The SDK tool runner drives the lookup loop; structured outputs (messages.parse + zod against the canonical itinerary schema) guarantee schema-conformant plans. Do NOT send the effort parameter (unsupported on Haiku). Deterministic LLMPort fakes in tests.

Acceptance: allocator is a pure domain function (exhaustively tested, integer minor units); plan->book conversion events emitted (PMF metric); L3 test walks describe-trip -> allocated plan -> quote -> book against sandbox mocks with state-delta assertions.

Depends on: seed-0001, seed-0002, seed-0003, seed-0004.

title: seed-0005 fix: INV-028 -- booking must not rely on in-process supplier-quote state (serverless-correct hold)
body:
CRITICAL money-path defect from the PR #13 review (INV-028). Fixes the seed-0005 build on branch kitchen/fix-seed-0005-budget-quote-book (PR #13, DRAFT -- NOT merged; the code is NOT on main). Check out that branch, apply the fix, re-verify, and update PR #13 -- do NOT branch from main. Best fixed together with the sibling seed-0005 review tickets in ONE rework pass + one re-review.

PROBLEM: bookItinerary (packages/api/src/services/booking.ts:300) calls port.book(quoteRow.supplierQuoteId) and depends on the sandbox engine's in-process `quotes` Map (packages/supply-adapter/src/sandbox/engine.ts:76), which is populated only during the earlier QUOTE request and never re-established on book (verifiedSupplyCatalog runs only in the quote flow; register() repopulates offers, not quotes). Under INV-028 (apps/web is stateless Vercel serverless) quote and book are SEPARATE invocations -> the map is empty at book -> every component returns unknown_quote -> every booking returns failed. The compose/L3 green evidence cannot detect this: the compose stack is a single long-lived process and the L3 happy path shares one container instance. Same in-process cross-request state class that was reverted in PR #10, now on the money path.

FIX (ARCHITECTURAL -> route through Spec Kit; update specs/005-budget-quote-book plan): make the supplier-hold handshake serverless-correct -- persist/reconstruct it outside process memory (e.g. the sandbox engine rehydrates its quotes from the persisted booking_quote rows on book), OR re-establish the hold on the book invocation with price+expiry reconciliation. Add an L3 test that books a hold from a FRESH container instance WITHOUT re-quoting and asserts success -- the exact Vercel quote->book sequence the current suite omits (COVERAGE gap the reviewers flagged).
notes:
Filed from PR #13 review (pr-auditor caught it; codex missed it; operator verified against engine.ts + booking.ts). Depends on: seed-0005 branch.
Kitchen Loop iteration 3 execute: fixed in one rework pass with seed-0005b/c on PR #13 branch (commits fe10035 + 409b4a1). INV-028 hold re-establishment (research D11) + fresh-container L3 test; live restart-repro witnessed BOOK_CONFIRMED 3/3 after docker compose restart web. Gates: vitest 193/193 in-image (9 L3 vs real Postgres), eslint/typecheck/depcruise clean, smoke 13/13, e2e 5/5, log scan clean. UAT PASS (7/7 steps, pinned worktree 409b4a1, integrity clean).

title: seed-0005 fix: duplicate quoteRowIds double-record money (atomic consume + unique constraint)
body:
BLOCKING money-path bug from the PR #13 review (INV-011 / FR-009). Fixes the seed-0005 build on branch kitchen/fix-seed-0005-budget-quote-book (PR #13, DRAFT -- NOT merged; the code is NOT on main). Check out that branch, apply the fix, re-verify, and update PR #13 -- do NOT branch from main. Best fixed together with the sibling seed-0005 review tickets in ONE rework pass + one re-review.

PROBLEM: duplicate quoteRowIds in one book request double-record money. bookInputSchema (booking.ts:42) does not dedupe quoteRowIds; bookItinerary iterates the raw input array (booking.ts:280); the consumed-guard reads a pre-transaction snapshot (booking.ts:286); the consume UPDATE has no `WHERE consumed_at IS NULL` predicate (booking.ts:366-369); and there is no unique constraint on booking_component.quoteRowId. A request [id, id] yields 2x booking_component + 2x markup_ledger + 2x PMF booking_confirmed (GBV inflation), violating FR-009 (a quote is consumed by at most one booking) and INV-011 conservation. The same root also permits concurrent double-consume.

FIX (bug-sized -- direct fix + repro test): dedupe quoteRowIds on input; make consume atomic (UPDATE booking_quote SET consumed_at=now() WHERE id=? AND consumed_at IS NULL, and only record the component if it affected a row); add a migration for a UNIQUE constraint on booking_component.quoteRowId; add an L2/L3 repro test that books the same hold twice (duplicate input AND a second request) and asserts exactly one set of rows + conserved money.
notes:
Filed from PR #13 review (codex caught it as blocking via the duplicate-input vector; pr-auditor flagged the same root as a concurrency race). Depends on: seed-0005 branch.
Kitchen Loop iteration 3 execute: fixed on PR #13 (fe10035) — input dedupe, atomic consume-first tx (WHERE consumed_at IS NULL), UNIQUE on booking_component.quote_row_id (verified live in Postgres); L3 repro tests: duplicate ids once + concurrent race one-winner. UAT card step 6 witnesses refuse-rebook live. Shares the seed-0005a rework pass.

title: seed-0005 fix: money-path conservation under concurrency — compensate lost-race supplier booking (FR-009/FR-011)
body:
BLOCKING money-path finding from the PR #13 FINAL tribunal (Codex Stage 4a, cross-model). Fixes the seed-0005 build on branch kitchen/fix-seed-0005-budget-quote-book (PR #13, DRAFT -- NOT merged; code is NOT on main). Check out that branch, apply the fix, re-verify, update PR #13 -- do NOT branch from main. Best fixed in one pass with the existing PR #13 rework.

PROBLEM: in bookItinerary (packages/api/src/services/booking.ts) the supplier port.book() is called (~L318/L359) BEFORE the atomic DB consume (~L394, UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL). Under two concurrent fresh-process invocations booking the SAME hold, BOTH re-establish + book at the supplier (each re-quotes to a DISTINCT fresh quoteId, so sandbox book-idempotency keyed on quoteId does NOT dedupe them), then only one wins the consume; the loser writes no DB rows and is retyped already_consumed (~L470). Result: a REAL supplier booking with NO booking_component/markup_ledger/PMF record -- an unrecorded external booking. Violates FR-009 ('consumed by at most one booking'), FR-011/INV-011 money-path conservation. Inert under the sandbox today (in-memory, expires) but a real integrity gap the instant a live adapter lands. Disclosed as research.md D11, but the 'defer to real adapter' framing is UNNECESSARY: the supply port ALREADY exposes cancel() (sandbox implements it), so compensation is buildable now.

FIX (money-path, SDD -- L3 conservation test MANDATORY): make the money path conserve under concurrency. Preferred: RESERVE-THEN-BOOK -- atomically flip consumed_at to claim the hold BEFORE calling port.book so only the winner books; release the reservation on book failure. Alternative: keep book-first but COMPENSATE -- for every component retyped already_consumed after the tx, call port.cancel(supplierBookingId) so no unrecorded external booking survives. Add an L3 test: two concurrent fresh-process books of one hold => exactly one confirmed booking, one booking_component/ledger/PMF set, and the supplier ends with exactly one live booking (loser cancelled) -- full state conservation on the failure branch. Update research.md D11 to reflect the wired compensation.
notes: Filed from PR #13 final tribunal: Codex REQUEST_CHANGES (blocking, FR-009/FR-011 conservation); pr-auditor rated it non-blocking (disclosed D11 deferral). Operator adjudication 2026-07-08: BLOCKING on the money path -- the compensation primitive (port.cancel) already exists, so it is fixable now, not real-adapter-blocked; the repo mandates state-conservation on money-path FAILURE branches. Depends on: seed-0005 branch (kitchen/fix-seed-0005-budget-quote-book). Sits above seed-0006 (marketplace) which depends on a conserving booking money path. | seed-0005d reserve-then-book landed on PR #13 branch (1c558d6), UAT 9/9, Codex confirmed the concurrency finding resolved. Blocked only by seed-0005e (expiry TOCTOU) before PR #13 can merge.

title: seed-0005 fix: enforce hold expiry atomically in the claim gate (FR-009 TOCTOU)
body:
BLOCKING money-path finding from the PR #13 final tribunal (Codex Stage 4a, cross-model). Fixes seed-0005 on branch kitchen/fix-seed-0005-budget-quote-book (PR #13, DRAFT -- NOT on main). Check out that branch, apply the fix, re-verify, update PR #13 -- do NOT branch from main.

PROBLEM (TOCTOU on expiry): bookItinerary checks expiry once in Phase 1 with Date.now() (booking.ts ~:292/:307), but the reserve/claim transaction gates only on consumed_at IS NULL (~:329/:338). If a persisted hold crosses expires_at while waiting on the claim lock (or before re-establishment), the unknown_quote path can take a FRESH supplier quote and port.book() (~:371-413) WITHOUT re-checking persisted expiry -- booking an expired hold. Violates FR-009 'at or past expiry MUST never be consumed/booked'. Low economic impact (price is re-matched and supplier-honored; sandbox-only at P0) but a real spec/lifecycle violation on the money path.

FIX (money-path, SDD -- L3 test mandatory): make expiry atomic with the claim. Add an expiry predicate to the claim UPDATE gate: WHERE consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > <now> (so an expired hold can never be claimed), and re-check now < expires_at in the re-establish branch before re-quoting/booking. Add an L3 test: a hold that expires between the Phase-1 check and the claim/book is refused (quote_expired), never booked, zero delta -- state conserved. Keep the existing concurrency behaviour (reserve-then-book + compensation) intact.
notes: Filed from PR #13 final tribunal (Codex REQUEST_CHANGES, High VIOLATION FR-009). Codex CONFIRMED the seed-0005d concurrency fix (reserve-then-book) is resolved and all prior fixes (INV-028/dedupe/unique/markupOf) hold; this is the sole remaining blocker. Depends on: seed-0005 branch. Sits above seed-0006. | DOWNGRADED to low (operator rule 2026-07-09): real but low-impact edge (no money loss, price re-matched + supplier-honored, sandbox-only at P0, microsecond race). Not merge-blocking. PR #13 merged with seed-0005; fix this via a normal iteration branch off main.

title: Marketplace v0: list/license/white-label + revenue-share plumbing (Constitution I/VI)
body:
Feature-sized — route through Spec Kit. The P0 Trade layer — Constitution I ("the trade layer is the moat") and Principle VI (revenue-share / client-ownership enforcement). This is the P0 marketplace pillar the other seeds do not build toward.

Build the minimal two-sided marketplace so the bootstrap sequence deterministically reaches the constitution P0 liquidity milestone ("basic marketplace where vetted agents list and other agents license/white-label trips; ratings + revenue-share plumbing", milestone: live liquidity in 1-2 destination niches):
- List a finished canonical itinerary (seed-0002 schema) as a marketplace listing with license terms
- License / white-label flow: a reseller agent licenses a listing and receives a rebranded copy whose provenance (original author, license terms, revenue-share obligations, rebrand lineage) travels with the itinerary (INV-002)
- Ratings on agents / listings
- Revenue-share plumbing recorded in the transaction path, in the same DB transaction as the license (INV-012); money math is pure integer-minor-unit in packages/domain

Lives in packages/marketplace (uses domain, itinerary-schema, ports; no supplier API shapes leak). Marketplace seller/reseller are relationships on a listing, not auth roles.

Acceptance: L3 test walks list -> license/white-label -> rate against sandbox state, with revenue-share ledger state-delta and money-path conservation assertions on the failure branch (no orphan ledger rows).

title: spec-gap: item-level booking exclusivity — two live holds on the same itinerary item can double-book it
body:
SPEC-SILENT finding from PR #13 review (pr-auditor Stage 3, 2026-07-08). The spec/contract for 005-budget-quote-book are silent on ITEM-level booking exclusivity: contracts/planner-and-booking.md §4 lists no item-uniqueness validation and spec.md's edge case covers only 'booking the same quote twice'.

OBSERVED BEHAVIOR (packages/api/src/services/booking.ts): quoteItinerary mints fresh holds for every bookable item on every call (only already_booked items are skipped, ~booking.ts:165-167), and bookItinerary validates tenant/unconsumed/unexpired but never checks whether the ITEM already has a booking_component (~booking.ts:297-378). Two quote calls before booking → two live holds per item; booking both records two components + two ledger rows for the same itinerary item. The UNIQUE backstop is per quote row only (schema.ts booking_component.quote_row_id), and the quote-time alreadyBooked read (~booking.ts:148-155) is not serialized against a concurrent book commit.

WHY SPEC-SILENT (not a code fix ticket): the code implements the spec as written; the spec does not define item exclusivity. Per the double-loop split, the SPEC evolves through SDD — amend spec.md/contracts §4 to define item-level exclusivity semantics, then implement the guard.

CANDIDATE GUARD (for the amendment to evaluate): partial unique index on booking_component (itinerary_id, item_id), or a book-time item-already-booked check inside the consume transaction.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
  1. spec.md + contracts/planner-and-booking.md §4 amended (via speckit flow, operator review per DIRECTIVE #3) to define item-level booking exclusivity.
  2. Guard implemented per the amended spec with an L3 test: two live holds on the same item, book both → exactly one booking_component + one ledger row; loser gets a typed failure; state conserved.

title: Money-path claim gate deadlocks under concurrent multi-component booking (40P01, intermittent)
body:
Bug-sized money-path finding from the iteration-3 execute in-image test run (seed-0009a cycle) — fix in its OWN cycle (money path, never co-bundled; L3 test mandatory).

PROBLEM: one full-suite vitest run vs the compose Postgres failed with `error: deadlock detected` (40P01) inside bookItinerary's claim transaction (packages/api/src/services/booking.ts ~:349-352): 'Process 303 waits for ShareLock on transaction 1017; blocked by process 301. Process 301 waits for ShareLock on transaction 1018; blocked by process 303. … while locking tuple in relation booking_quote'. Two concurrent book requests claiming overlapping booking_quote rows acquire row locks in inconsistent order → Postgres kills one tx. The L3 concurrency race test (l3-booking) is the witness; re-runs green (1 failure in 3 suite runs; file alone 16/16 green) — an interleaving-dependent flake, likely surfaced by the added parallel L3 file shifting worker timing.

IMPACT: (a) live API can return an untyped 500 (deadlock) instead of the typed already_consumed loser outcome when two agents book the same holds concurrently — state stays conserved (tx rollback + seed-0005d supplier compensation), so it is an AVAILABILITY/typed-failure gap, not money loss; (b) the flake destabilizes the regression oracle (`pnpm test` can go red with no product change).

FIX DIRECTION: make claim lock order deterministic — e.g. process/lock quoteRowIds in a canonical sort order (and/or a single UPDATE … WHERE id = ANY(sorted ids) so Postgres locks in one statement), or SELECT … FOR UPDATE with ORDER BY id before the per-row consume. Keep reserve-then-book + compensation semantics intact (seed-0005d/e). Add/extend an L3 test that books two overlapping multi-component holds concurrently N times and asserts no 40P01 and one typed winner/loser split; conservation assertions on both branches.

WITNESS: .kitchenloop/evidence/iter-3/seed-0009a/compose-logs.txt line ~88 (postgres deadlock ERROR, 2026-07-09 13:33:56 UTC) + the failed vitest run in the iter-3 execute transcript. body:

Source: the recovered zero-context uat-evaluator run for seed-0009d (evidence /tmp/uat-seed-0009d/.kitchenloop/uat-runs/seed-0009d/evidence.md, verdict PRODUCT_FAIL; recovered by ticket loop-uat-gate-comment-missing, report docs/internal/reports/uat-gate-comment-investigation.md).

COUNTER-WITNESS: the operator's hand-run of the SAME sealed card at the SAME HEAD had 7.5% stick (PASS 12/12, .kitchenloop/uat-runs/seed-0009d/evidence.md). So the failure is interaction-dependent.

CODE READING: apps/web/app/(workspace)/marketplace/marketplace-panel.tsx:101-122 — values are NOT reset on a refused submission (setValues(INITIAL_FORM) runs only on success), and the input is a controlled component (value={values.sharePercent}, onChange wired). The snap-back is the classic symptom of a fill that never committed to React state: the refusal re-render restores the state value ('10') over the uncommitted DOM value ('7.5'). Two hypotheses: (a) PRODUCT — some real input paths (autofill, password managers, certain fill mechanisms) skip the events React needs, so a real seller's declared terms can be silently replaced by the default on the money/trust path (Constitution VI: recorded split must match declared terms); (b) TOOLING — Playwright-MCP's fill on this number input doesn't commit, i.e. an evaluator-environment artifact that will keep producing false PRODUCT_FAILs on future UAT cards.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. Deterministic repro attempt: an e2e spec fills 7.5 via Playwright fill(), submits pre-vetting (refused), re-submits post-vetting, asserts the listing card shows '7.5% revenue share'; plus a manual/MCP-driven variant matching the evaluator's fill technique.
  2. If (a) PRODUCT: fix so the declared share survives a refused submission regardless of fill path (e.g. read the submitted value from the form event, or re-assert DOM value into state on submit), with the repro red-then-green; ESCALATE priority to high/critical.
  3. If (b) TOOLING: document the hazard in the ticket + loop memory, and the fix proposal for card-writing guidance goes to the operator (UAT protocol is sealed).
  4. Either way: the listing flow's declared-terms integrity gets a pinned regression test.

Depends on: seed-0009d (merged, PR #27). Related: seed-0009d-a (rating/deactivate controls), desk row UAT-VERDICT-DURABILITY.

ESCALATED to high (execute, iter-3 batch cycle, 2026-07-10): hypothesis (a) PRODUCT confirmed — a DOM-set value with no committed input events reproduces the snap-back deterministically (tests/e2e/listing-terms-integrity.spec.ts); fix reads the form DOM at submit.

body:
## Description
Immediately after a successful license, the marketplace page shows the receipt ("...is now in your workspace") while the SAME page's "Sell a trip" panel still says "Nothing to list yet" (or, when already populated, its picker lacks the new white-label copy) until a full page reload. The browse panel refreshes without reload (FR-011); the sell-form's itinerary projection does not. Iteration-3 report BUG-3.

## Root Cause Hypothesis
`MarketplacePanel.handleLicense` success path refreshes only the listings (`await loadListings()`); it never re-runs `loadItineraries()`, so the `picker` state (fed by `workspace.itinerary.list`) keeps its mount-time snapshot. The white-label copy created by the license mutation is invisible to the sell form until remount.

## File Pointers
- `apps/web/app/(workspace)/marketplace/marketplace-panel.tsx:125-152` — handleLicense success calls only loadListings(); needs loadItineraries() too
- `apps/web/app/(workspace)/marketplace/marketplace-panel.tsx:78-90` — loadItineraries() runs mount-only via useEffect
- `apps/web/app/(workspace)/marketplace/marketplace-panel.tsx:305-312` — the "Nothing to list yet" empty state seen post-license

3. As B, license A's listing -> receipt renders "is now in your workspace"

## Expected Behavior
On license success the sell-form picker refreshes in place: the new white-label copy is pickable without a page reload, consistent with the receipt and the browse panel's FR-011 behavior.

## Actual Behavior
Picker keeps its mount-time snapshot ("Nothing to list yet" / stale option list) until manual reload.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After a successful license, the sell-form picker contains the new white-label copy without a page reload
- [ ] The empty state is replaced in place when the first copy arrives

title: Unparseable stored itinerary turns every read surface into a raw 500 — including the client share link
body:
## Description
A stored itinerary document that fails canonical re-validation (parseItinerary ZodError) produces raw INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR 500s with stack traces in compose logs on every read surface: workspace.itinerary.get, the public clientView.itinerary, and the traveler-facing /view/<token> SSR page. Spec 010 promises typed unavailable states ("not_found is a payload, never an error ... the unavailable state reveals nothing"), and the share link is a durable URL in a client's inbox. Any document the current schema refuses (a legacy document after a schema evolution, a bad migration, operator surgery) turns that client-held link into a crash page, and the owning agent has no way to see WHICH document is broken or why. Iteration-3 report (second pass) BUG-b1.

The refusal itself is CORRECT (INV-001 boundary re-validation; the D-006.c closed enum held on every surface) — its SHAPE is the bug.

## Root Cause Hypothesis
parseItinerary throws ZodError uncaught at the read-path call sites; tRPC/Next map the throw to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR + stack. No catch layer distinguishes "document fails re-validation" from a genuine server fault:
- packages/api/src/services/booking.ts:151 (itineraryOverview -> workspace.itinerary.get)
- packages/api/src/services/client-view.ts:231 (share-link resolve -> clientView.itinerary -> /view SSR)
(Marketplace write paths — listings.ts:70, licensing.ts:103/111 — throwing on a WRITE is acceptable fail-closed, but should share the typed-refusal shape where user-facing.)

## File Pointers
- packages/api/src/services/booking.ts:151 — parseItinerary in itineraryOverview (agent get path)
- packages/api/src/services/client-view.ts:231 — parseItinerary on the share-link resolve path
- packages/api/src/routers/itinerary.ts:27-34 — get: only not_found is typed today
- packages/api/src/routers/client-view.ts — public procedure returning the payload
- apps/web/app/(client-view)/view/[token]/page.tsx — SSR page consuming the payload (renders the crash today)
- scenarios/incubating/content-library-media-gap/scenario.mjs — live witness (boundary checks green; the refusal SHAPE is the bug)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Boot the live compose stack (keyless/FakeLLM fine); sign up, draft an itinerary, mint a share link.
2. Corrupt the stored document past the schema, e.g.: UPDATE itinerary SET document = jsonb_set(document, '{media}', '[{"id":"x","kind":"image","storageKey":"k","source":"scraped-web","alt":"a"}]'::jsonb) WHERE id = '<id>';
3. GET /view/<token> -> 500 crash page; workspace.itinerary.get -> INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; clientView.itinerary -> INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; compose log carries a ZodError stack.

## Expected Behavior
- Traveler surfaces (clientView.itinerary, /view): typed not_found/unavailable payload — reveals nothing, never a crash page (spec 010).
- Owning agent (workspace.itinerary.get): typed diagnostic naming the itinerary and that it fails current-schema validation (safe summary, not a raw stack).
- Log: one structured warn line (itinerary id + zod issue summary), no stack dump.

## Actual Behavior
Raw 500s on all three surfaces; ZodError stack in compose logs; the agent gets no diagnostic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] L3 test: arranged invalid document -> clientView.itinerary returns the typed unavailable payload (no throw), /view renders a branded unavailable state, workspace.itinerary.get returns a typed diagnostic
- [ ] No stack trace in compose logs for this class; a single structured warn instead
- [ ] The typed unavailable state reveals nothing about the document (spec 010 — no existence-oracle change)
- [ ] scenarios/incubating/content-library-media-gap checks extended to pin the typed shape (do not weaken existing green checks)
- [ ] Regression test added covering this scenario

1. Media storage port + derived tables (INV-025: the itinerary carries only refs; binaries live in Postgres-derived tables/CDN via packages/db) — a MediaStorePort in the supply-adapter port family with a local/compose implementation.
2. Agency media library API (workspace.media.*): upload (agent-upload), register licensed stock (licensed-stock), list — tenant-scoped (INV-004), source enum enforced at the boundary.

Scope gap, not a defect: seed-0002 landed the full MediaRef model in the canonical schema, but no seed ever covered the storage port, library API, attach surface, or rendering. The trust-boundary allowlist correctly keeps media out of the client view until it is deliberately projected.

title: Client view prices a booked trip at the agency's confidential net rates

## Description
Share a BOOKED itinerary and the traveler-facing /view/<token> page prices every item at the agency's confidential NET rates. Observed live: client page shows trip total 347.80 USD while the booking confirmation for the same trip shows 424.31 USD of client prices (delta = exactly the 22% markup); per-item DB probe confirms document.pricing.sellPrice == pricing.netRate on all 6 items. The traveler reads the agency's exact cost basis (margin exposure — the share panel promises "your brand, your prices"), and the contractual booked price mismatches the page beside a "Booked" badge. Affects ORIGINALS exactly as licensed copies — the reseller journey just made the markup delta visible. Iteration-3 report (third pass) BUG-1; the Codex feasibility check predicted the seam.

## Root Cause Hypothesis
Three locally-correct pieces compose broken:
1. packages/domain/src/assemble.ts:166 — draft-time `pricing = { netRate: priced, sellPrice: priced }` ("markup applies at quote time (FR-007)") — a placeholder nothing ever updates;
2. the quote/book flow computes the real sell (net x markup) into booking_quote/booking_component/markup_ledger but never writes it back to the canonical document;
3. spec 010 deliberately projects the document's stored sellPrice (spec.md:216 "it does not re-quote live inventory") — written for the un-booked case, silent on the booked case.
The canonical schema itself documents the violated contract: packages/itinerary-schema/src/item.ts:16 — sellPrice is "client-facing (net + agency markup)".

## Routing
Product fix + spec amendment through the speckit flow (specs/005-budget-quote-book + specs/010-client-view-share): either stamp the booked sell into the document at book time, or project booked-component sells at read time. NOT ALWAYS-HALT — no canonical schema version bump (the field and its semantics already exist in v0.1.0) and no revenue-share/client-ownership change — but the chosen fix touches the canonical document write path (or the trust-boundary read projection), so the plan MUST state which option and pass the Constitution Check; the spec amendment gets operator review inside the speckit flow (DIRECTIVE item 3). Money-adjacent: L3 integration tests mandatory.
Folded in (same pass, FEAT-1): once the storage question is settled, the client view should distinguish estimated vs confirmed/contractual prices for booked items rather than one undifferentiated price field plus a badge.

## File Pointers

The traveler-facing view of a booked trip shows the client (sell) prices the booking recorded — never the agency's net cost; sellPrice honors its documented semantics once a markup is realized.

## Actual Behavior
Client-view totals equal the net rates; the booked sell exists only in booking tables/markup_ledger; the document keeps the draft placeholder.

title: Marketplace: seller's own-card revenue-share badge implies it governs first-sale earnings, but it doesn't
body:
## Description
On a seller's own marketplace listing card, the "X% revenue share" badge sits
directly beside the "N licenses · Y earned" first-sale earnings figure
(`apps/web/app/(workspace)/marketplace/marketplace-panel.tsx:265` and
`:268-272`). A seller reasonably reads these as cause-and-effect ("I declared
20%, so I earn 20% of the fee"), but the declared `revenueShareBps` currently
governs NOTHING on the first-sale path — first-sale earnings always use the
platform-wide fixed `DEFAULT_PLATFORM_TAKE_RATE_BPS = 1000`
(`packages/marketplace/src/config.ts:6`, consumed in
`packages/marketplace/src/licensing.ts:113`), so every seller nets a flat 90%
regardless of what they typed. The listing-form copy right above
("...enforces your revenue share on every license",
`marketplace-panel.tsx:230-231`) reinforces the same false impression at
creation time.

Observed live during iteration-4 ideate (seed-0030 stress test): a listing
declared "5% revenue share" earned 90.0% of its fee (270.00 of 300.00 USD);
a listing declared "20% revenue share" would earn the identical 90% if
licensed. Not a money bug — the math is exactly per spec 006/014 and the
earnings aggregation itself was verified correct — this is a presentation/
copy issue: the UI juxtaposes two independently-computed numbers in a way
that invites a wrong causal reading, for every seller, on every listing,
whether or not resale semantics are ever wired up.

Distinct from the open OPERATOR-DESK RESALE-SHARE-SEMANTICS item: that item
is about whether the declared share should someday govern money on a RESALE
(operator decision, DIRECTIVE ALWAYS-HALT — money-semantics). This ticket is
about relabeling/repositioning UI copy on the FIRST-sale card so it stops
implying a causal link that already doesn't exist today. It requires no
change to money math, the canonical schema, or revenue-share semantics, so
it is in-scope for the loop to execute directly (no operator gate needed).

## Root Cause Hypothesis
`marketplace-panel.tsx`'s `ListingCard` component renders the seller's
declared `revenueShareBps` badge (spec 011 contract) and the seller's actual
first-sale earnings (spec 014, seed-0030) as adjacent, visually-parallel
elements with no copy distinguishing "declared, for future resale" from
"actual, this sale's platform take-rate is fixed." The two values come from
unrelated code paths (`formatShareBps(listing.revenueShareBps)` — the
seller's own listing input — vs. `formatEarnings(licenseCount,
sellerCreditTotalMinor, currency)` — server-aggregated from
`revenue_share_ledger.sellerCreditMinor`, itself computed at license time
via the fixed `DEFAULT_PLATFORM_TAKE_RATE_BPS`), but nothing in the render
signals that to the seller.

## File Pointers
- `apps/web/app/(workspace)/marketplace/marketplace-panel.tsx:265` — the
  `X% revenue share` badge (declared `revenueShareBps`, currently inert on
  first sale)
- `apps/web/app/(workspace)/marketplace/marketplace-panel.tsx:268-272` — the
  adjacent first-sale earnings line (`formatEarnings`, actual platform-take
  computed money)
- `apps/web/app/(workspace)/marketplace/marketplace-panel.tsx:230-231` — the
  listing-form copy ("...enforces your revenue share on every license") that
  makes the same overpromise at creation time
- `packages/marketplace/src/config.ts:6` — `DEFAULT_PLATFORM_TAKE_RATE_BPS
  = 1000`, the fixed first-sale platform take rate that actually governs
  earnings regardless of the declared share
- `packages/marketplace/src/licensing.ts:113` — first-sale split uses
  `DEFAULT_PLATFORM_TAKE_RATE_BPS`, never `listing.revenueShareBps`
- `packages/marketplace/src/marketplace-flow.ts` (`formatShareBps`,
  `formatEarnings`) — the two independent formatting helpers feeding the
  juxtaposed card fields

## Reproduction Steps
1. Boot the stack: `docker compose down -v && docker compose up --build --wait`
2. Sign up/in as a seller agency, draft an itinerary, list it on the
   marketplace declaring an arbitrary "revenue share %" (e.g. 20%)
3. Have a different agency license the listing
4. Reload `/marketplace` as the seller and view the listing card: observe
   the "20% revenue share" badge sitting beside "1 · 90% of fee earned"
   (`formatEarnings` shows the seller actually nets the fixed 90% platform
   take, not 80%/20% implied by the badge)

## Expected Behavior
The first-sale card should not visually imply that the declared
`revenueShareBps` explains or governs the adjacent earnings figure, since
it currently governs nothing on first sale.

## Actual Behavior
The declared-share badge and the actual-earnings figure are rendered as
adjacent, visually-parallel elements with no distinguishing copy, inviting
a seller to (incorrectly) read them as cause-and-effect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The seller's own listing card no longer implies the declared revenue
      share explains the adjacent first-sale earnings figure (via
      relabeling, repositioning, or an explanatory caption/tooltip such as
      "applies to future resales")
- [ ] The listing-form copy at `marketplace-panel.tsx:230-231` is reworded
      to stop promising that the declared share "enforces...on every
      license" when it currently only applies to a not-yet-wired resale path
- [ ] No change to `DEFAULT_PLATFORM_TAKE_RATE_BPS`, `licensing.ts` split
      math, the canonical schema, or any money-semantics code — copy/
      presentation only
- [ ] Existing L3/e2e marketplace tests (earnings, licensing, listing-card
      rendering) still pass unchanged
- [ ] Regression test/assertion added covering the updated copy (e.g. an
      e2e or component assertion that the badge text or nearby caption no
      longer reads as first-sale-causal)

## Source

- Report: docs/internal/reports/iteration-4-report.md
- Scenario: seller-multi-listing-earnings-isolation (T2 Composition)
- Tier: T2

## Priority Score
- Severity: 1 (cosmetic/confusing copy, no money bug, no functional break)
- Frequency: 3 (every seller sees this on every listing with a non-default
  declared share)
- Fix effort: 3 (copy/relabel change only, no money-math or schema touch)
- **Total: 7/9**

title: Coverage matrix and loop-state.md silently disagree on combos tested
body:
## Description
`.kitchenloop/coverage-matrix.yaml` and `docs/internal/loop-state.md` both claim to report "combos tested" but drift out of sync with each other and with the actual scenario files under `scenarios/incubating/`. At iteration-4 ideate time the matrix showed 17/36 tested combos; `loop-state.md`'s iteration-3 regression section claimed 30/36 with a different list of remaining gaps; neither matched what the 6 iteration-3 scenario scripts actually exercised. The matrix has a self-documented artifact-loss note (top of `coverage-matrix.yaml`: "the iteration-3 FIRST-pass update... was lost with the iter-3 regress artifacts (REGRESS-ARTIFACT-LOSS class) -- backfilled... from the landed iteration-3 report") but `loop-state.md`'s number carries no equivalent staleness flag, so there's no single trustworthy source for "what have we actually tested." The iteration-4 ideate pass had to read all 6 `scenarios/incubating/*/scenario.mjs` files by hand to find the real coverage gap (itinerary-builder x {web,api} x agent-reseller), costing real ideate time.

## Root Cause Hypothesis
`coverage-matrix.yaml` is hand-maintained by the ideate phase (appends `tested:` entries) and hand-summarized by the regress phase into `loop-state.md`'s prose ("Coverage" section) -- two independently hand-authored representations of the same fact with no derivation link between them, so they can silently diverge whenever one is updated without the other (as happened when the iter-3 regress artifacts were lost mid-iteration, per the matrix's own artifact-loss note). There is no mechanism that derives the coverage count from a machine-readable witness in the scenario files themselves.

## File Pointers
- `.kitchenloop/coverage-matrix.yaml:1-18` -- the artifact-loss note and hand-maintained `tested:` list
- `docs/internal/loop-state.md:61` -- iteration-3 "Coverage" prose section (30/36, found stale/inconsistent with the matrix)
- `scenarios/incubating/*/scenario.mjs` -- the actual witnesses; none currently declare a structured coverage-claim header the matrix/loop-state could derive from
- `.claude/skills/kitchenloop-regress/` -- the phase that writes the loop-state.md Coverage section (candidate site for a derivation step)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Read `.kitchenloop/coverage-matrix.yaml`'s `tested_combos`/`coverage_pct` header.
2. Read `docs/internal/loop-state.md`'s most recent "Coverage" section for the same iteration.
3. Compare both numbers/gap-lists against a manual read of every `scenarios/incubating/*/scenario.mjs` file.
4. Observe the three sources disagree (as they did at iteration-4 ideate time: matrix 17/36, loop-state 30/36, actual-file-read gap list different from both).

## Expected Behavior
There is exactly one trustworthy source (or a mechanically-derived one) for "which spec-surface combos have been tested," so ideate does not need to hand-read every scenario file to find real gaps.

## Actual Behavior
Two hand-maintained artifacts (coverage-matrix.yaml, loop-state.md prose) can silently disagree with each other and with the underlying scenario files, with only one of the two carrying a self-documented staleness flag.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each `scenarios/incubating/*/scenario.mjs` (or its README) declares a structured, machine-parseable coverage-claim (feature x platform x user_type x result) that a tool can extract
- [ ] `coverage-matrix.yaml`'s `tested_combos`/`coverage_pct` (or its replacement) is derived from those declarations rather than hand-appended
- [ ] `loop-state.md`'s "Coverage" section either reads from the same derived source or is removed in favor of pointing at the matrix, so the two can no longer disagree
- [ ] A regress-phase re-run after a scenario file changes updates the derived coverage automatically (no separate hand-edit step)

## Source

- Report: docs/internal/reports/iteration-4-report.md (Friction Point 1)
- Scenario: Reseller builds fresh (T2 Composition)

- Severity: 2 (annoying -- costs real ideate time to work around, not a product defect)
- Frequency: 3 (every ideate pass reads the coverage matrix to pick a scenario; this friction recurs every iteration)
- Fix effort: 2 (medium -- needs a structured coverage-claim convention + a derivation step in regress/ideate tooling)
- **Total: 7/9** -> high

title: Scenario idiom `held.map(i => i.quote)` silently drops itemId -- footgun for new scripts
body:
## Description
Two incubating L3 scenario scripts (`golden-path-trade-live`, `reseller-books-copy-live`) use the idiom `held = quote.data.items.filter(i => i.outcome === "held").map(i => i.quote)`, which flattens away each row's `itemId` and keeps only the nested `quote` object. This works for those two scripts because neither ever needs to correlate a held/booked row back to a specific canonical-document item. A new scenario author copying the idiom (this iteration's `reseller-builds-fresh` first draft) who *does* need per-item correlation (e.g. asserting price fidelity per document item, not just in aggregate) gets a silent collapse: `held.map(r => [r.itemId, ...])` produces `undefined` for every row, collapsing a 6-entry map down to size 1. The resulting assertion failure looks exactly like a product bug at first glance ("all 1 booked items show Booked... view shows 6 booked of 6") before it's traced back to the copied idiom rather than the product. `partially-booked-client-view` and the final `reseller-builds-fresh` script get this right by keeping the outer `{itemId, quote}` shape instead of unwrapping it.

## Root Cause Hypothesis
No shared helper or documented convention governs how incubating scenario scripts should shape the result of filtering `quote.data.items` by `outcome === "held"` -- each script independently chose whether to unwrap to `.quote` or keep `{itemId, quote}`, and the unwrapping choice is only safe for scripts that never need per-item correlation. Nothing in the two "unsafe" scripts flags that the shape drops `itemId`, so the choice isn't visible to someone copying the pattern.

## File Pointers
- `scenarios/incubating/golden-path-trade-live/scenario.mjs:138` -- `held = ...filter(...).map((i) => i.quote)` (drops itemId; safe here, no per-item correlation needed)
- `scenarios/incubating/reseller-books-copy-live/scenario.mjs:170` -- same idiom, same risk
- `scenarios/incubating/partially-booked-client-view/scenario.mjs:178-186` -- correct reference pattern, keeps the outer `{itemId, quote}` shape
- `scenarios/incubating/reseller-builds-fresh/scenario.mjs:179-180` -- this iteration's script, corrected during authoring to keep `{itemId, quote}` (comment at line 179: "only handle correlating a held/booked row back to its document item below")

## Reproduction Steps
1. Copy the idiom from `reseller-books-copy-live/scenario.mjs:170` into a new scenario script.
2. Add a per-item correlation step: `new Map(held.map(r => [r.itemId, r.quote.sellMinor]))`.
3. Observe the resulting Map has size 1 (all keys collapse to `undefined`) instead of one entry per held item.

## Expected Behavior
Either every incubating scenario script keeps the `{itemId, quote}` shape by default (so `itemId` is always available for correlation), or the two scripts that unwrap to `.quote` carry a one-line comment flagging that the shape drops `itemId` and is unsafe to copy for per-item correlation.

## Actual Behavior
Two scripts silently drop `itemId` with no comment; nothing distinguishes "safe to copy" from "unsafe to copy" at the call site.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `golden-path-trade-live/scenario.mjs:138` and `reseller-books-copy-live/scenario.mjs:170` either switch to the `{itemId, quote}` shape or gain a one-line comment noting the drop and pointing to the safe pattern
- [ ] No behavior change to either script's existing assertions (both scripts keep passing as-is)

## Source
- Iteration: 4
- Report: docs/internal/reports/iteration-4-report.md (Friction Point 2, Improvement IMP-1)
- Scenario: Reseller builds fresh (T2 Composition)

## Priority Score
- Severity: 1 (cosmetic -- a test-authoring footgun, not product-facing)
- Frequency: 2 (recurring pattern risk -- any future scenario author copying either script hits it)
- Fix effort: 3 (tiny -- one-line comment or shape change, under an hour)
- **Total: 6/9** -> medium

title: derive-coverage.mjs blind spot: doesn't scan tests/e2e/*.spec.ts KITCHENLOOP-COVERAGE blocks
body:
## Description
`scripts/kitchenloop/derive-coverage.mjs` (the seed-0031 fix — single-source-of-truth
coverage derivation) only scans `scenarios/incubating/*/scenario.mjs` for
`KITCHENLOOP-COVERAGE` blocks. It has no equivalent scan of `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts`.
Two Playwright specs already carry real, durable coverage of specific
feature x platform x user_type combos (`content-library-journey.spec.ts` for
`content-library x web x agent-seller`, `marketplace-journey.spec.ts` for
`marketplace x web x agent-reseller`) but the derived matrix has no way to see
them — they stayed invisible until the iteration-5 ideate pass manually
re-declared them inside an unrelated new scenario file's COVERAGE block,
because that was the only mechanism the tool understands. This is the exact
two-sources-of-truth problem seed-0031 was filed to fix, recurring in a new
location (e2e specs) that seed-0031's implementation didn't cover.

## Root Cause Hypothesis
`scripts/kitchenloop/derive-coverage.mjs` hardcodes `SCENARIOS_DIR =
scenarios/incubating` as its only input directory. It was written to fix
hand-authored drift between `coverage-matrix.yaml` and `loop-state.md` by
deriving from scenario scripts' own declarations, but the derivation walk
never got extended to the other place coverage is durably witnessed —
Playwright e2e specs under `tests/e2e/`. Any coverage a spec file earns by
existing there is invisible to the matrix unless a human notices and
re-declares it elsewhere.

## File Pointers
- `scripts/kitchenloop/derive-coverage.mjs:16-18` — `SCENARIOS_DIR` constant and the directory walk that needs a second source (`tests/e2e/`)
- `tests/e2e/content-library-journey.spec.ts` — carries real coverage (content-library x web x agent-seller) invisible to the matrix today
- `tests/e2e/marketplace-journey.spec.ts` — carries real coverage (marketplace x web x agent-reseller) invisible to the matrix today
- `scenarios/incubating/reseller-media-attach/scenario.mjs` — the iteration-5 scenario that had to manually re-declare both specs' coverage as a workaround

## Reproduction Steps
1. `git show main:tests/e2e/content-library-journey.spec.ts | head -20` — confirm no `KITCHENLOOP-COVERAGE` block scan targets this file.
2. `node scripts/kitchenloop/derive-coverage.mjs` and inspect the regenerated `.kitchenloop/coverage-matrix.yaml` — `content-library x web x agent-seller` and `marketplace x web x agent-reseller` are only present because `scenarios/incubating/reseller-media-attach/scenario.mjs` re-declares them, not because the e2e specs were scanned.
3. Delete that re-declaration and re-run — the two combos silently disappear from the matrix even though the passing e2e specs still exist and still cover them.

## Expected Behavior
`derive-coverage.mjs` scans both `scenarios/incubating/*/scenario.mjs` and `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` for `KITCHENLOOP-COVERAGE` blocks (adding the block convention to the e2e specs that don't have one yet), so a spec's coverage claim is visible from where it's actually witnessed instead of needing a human to re-declare it in an unrelated file.

## Actual Behavior
Coverage earned by `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` files is invisible to the derived matrix unless manually re-declared inside a `scenarios/incubating/*/scenario.mjs` file, reproducing the exact hand-maintained-drift risk seed-0031 fixed for the old hand-authored matrix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/e2e/content-library-journey.spec.ts` and `tests/e2e/marketplace-journey.spec.ts` each carry their own `KITCHENLOOP-COVERAGE` block
- [ ] `derive-coverage.mjs` walks `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts` in addition to `scenarios/incubating/*/scenario.mjs` and merges both sets of declarations into `coverage-matrix.yaml`
- [ ] Re-running `node scripts/kitchenloop/derive-coverage.mjs` after removing the iteration-5 workaround re-declaration still shows both combos as tested, sourced from the e2e specs directly
- [ ] Regression test / script self-check added so a future e2e spec without a COVERAGE block fails the same typo/malformed-block guard the scenario scripts already get

## Source
- Iteration: 5
- Report: docs/internal/reports/iteration-5-report.md (Friction Points / IMP-1)
- Scenario: Reseller attaches their own media to a licensed white-label copy
- Tier: T2

## Priority Score
- Severity: 2 (annoying — costs real ideate time, coverage matrix undercounts real coverage)
- Frequency: 3 (recurs every iteration that adds or relies on an e2e spec's coverage)
- Fix effort: 3 (small — extend an existing, working derivation script to a second glob + add two COVERAGE block comments)
- **Total: 8/9 -> high**

Related: seed-0031 (done, PR #46) — fixed the scenario-vs-loop-state drift; this ticket closes the same drift class for the e2e-spec case it didn't cover.

title: Open design question: should licensing register inherited gallery media into reseller's own library?
body:
## Description
When a reseller licenses a listing, the white-label copy's inherited gallery
media (copied from the seller's original document per seed-0023's ratified
transfer model) can be detached from the gallery, but can never be attached to
a specific itinerary item. The item-level attach picker sources its options
from `workspace.media.list` (the reseller's own registered library assets)
only — the inherited photo lives in the copied document's `media` array but
was never registered as a library row under the reseller's tenant, so it can
never appear in an item-level picker for them. Confirmed live: reseller
"Nomad Trails" licensed a Santorini trip carrying seller "Meridian Journeys"'s
gallery photo; the inherited photo showed in the gallery and could be
detached from it, but never appeared as an option when attaching media to the
Day-1 transfer item.

This is plausibly correct-by-design (INV-004 tenant-scoped library ownership
— a reseller's item-level picker should only offer assets THEY registered)
rather than a bug. It is filed as an open product question, not a defect.

## Root Cause Hypothesis
Two code paths read media from two different sources: the gallery/detach path
reads directly off the itinerary document's `media` array (tenant-agnostic —
whatever is in the copied document), while the item-level attach picker reads
`workspace.media.list` (tenant-scoped — only assets the CURRENT tenant
explicitly registered). Licensing (`whiteLabelCopy`,
`packages/marketplace/src/licensing.ts`) copies the document's `media` array
into the new copy but does not also insert a corresponding row into the
reseller's `workspace.media` library, so the inherited asset is visible/
detachable at the document level but invisible to any tenant-scoped picker.
Whether that's the intended shape of a white-label copy's media rights, or a
gap that should register inherited assets into the reseller's library too, is
an open question — not yet answered by seed-0023's transfer/strip/attribution
decision, which covered whether media travels with the copy at all, not
whether it becomes fully manipulable once it does.

## File Pointers
- `packages/marketplace/src/licensing.ts` — `whiteLabelCopy`, where inherited media is copied into the new document but not registered into `workspace.media`
- item-level attach picker component (web) — sources options from `workspace.media.list`, tenant-scoped
- gallery attach/detach path — operates directly on the document's `media` array, tenant-agnostic
- `packages/itinerary-schema/src/media.ts` — `MediaRef` shape; no field today distinguishes "inherited, gallery-only" from "owned, fully manipulable"
- seed-0023 (done, PR #50) — ratified the transfer/strip/attribution decision this ticket extends

## Reproduction Steps
1. As a vetted seller agency, draft an itinerary, attach a registered media asset to its gallery, list it on the marketplace.
2. As a second vetted reseller agency, license the listing.
3. Open the resulting white-label copy in `/workspace`; the inherited photo appears in the gallery and can be detached from it.
4. Attempt to attach the SAME inherited photo to a specific itinerary item (not the gallery) — it never appears as an option in the item-level attach picker, because it was never registered under `workspace.media.list` for the reseller's tenant.

## Expected Behavior
Undecided — this ticket's deliverable is the decision itself, not an implementation. Two candidate answers: (a) licensing also registers the seller's gallery assets into the reseller's own library (inherited media becomes fully manipulable, matching full editorial control already granted at the document level for attach/detach), or (b) "inherited but gallery-only" is the intended and final shape of a white-label copy's media rights (no further action needed).

## Actual Behavior
Inherited gallery media is document-level manipulable (attach/detach on the gallery) but invisible to the tenant-scoped item-level attach picker, an inconsistency between two media-editing surfaces that a reseller can hit on any white-label copy carrying seller-registered media.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Operator decision recorded (DIRECTIVE item 3 — spec amendments go through speckit with review): does licensing register inherited gallery assets into the reseller's own library, or is "gallery-movable only" the final intended shape?
- [ ] If (a): a speckit spec amendment describing the registration step, its tenant/rights implications, and a follow-up implementation ticket
- [ ] If (b): the current behavior is documented as intentional (e.g. a comment or spec note at `licensing.ts`'s `whiteLabelCopy`) so it isn't re-flagged as a bug by a future ideate pass
- [ ] Either way, the decision references seed-0023 so both media-rights questions (does it transfer at all vs. how manipulable is it once transferred) resolve into one coherent rights model

## Source
- Iteration: 5
- Report: docs/internal/reports/iteration-5-report.md (Missing Features / FEAT-1)
- Scenario: Reseller attaches their own media to a licensed white-label copy
- Tier: T2

## Priority Score
- Severity: 2 (no user-visible defect today, but an inconsistent editorial-control story across two media surfaces on every media-bearing licensed trade)
- Frequency: 2 (every licensed trade of a media-bearing itinerary where the reseller wants item-level placement, not just gallery placement)
- Fix effort: 2 (design/spec decision, hours — matches seed-0023's own effort scoring for the same class of question)
- **Total: 6/9 -> medium**

Related: seed-0023 (done, PR #50) — ratified transfer/strip/attribution for licensed media; this ticket is the follow-on question seed-0023 left open (manipulability once transferred, not transfer itself).

title: Dashboard app shell — replace the single-column 'typeform' with a real product workspace (sidebar nav + agent home)

title: Conversational AI itinerary editing — chat to add/remove/replace places + inline hotel suggestions (A2/A5)
body:
OPERATOR (verbatim): 'AI itinerary builder. Not just AI building it. Chatting with the agent to add or remove certain places.' Today the flow is strictly one-shot: a form -> a single streamed draft (routers/itinerary.ts draft SSE), with NO refine/chat/addItem/removeItem procedure. This is the single biggest 'AI agent' gap.

BUILD multi-turn conversational refinement on top of an existing draft:
1. A chat panel beside the itinerary where the user types natural-language edit requests: 'add a food tour on day 2', 'remove the museum', 'swap the hotel for something boutique near the water', 'make day 3 cheaper'. The LLM (behind LLMPort; FakeLLM must give deterministic sensible edits for the keyless demo) interprets the request and returns a structured mutation applied to the canonical itinerary schema (add/remove/replace items, re-balance budget). Stream the assistant's reply + show the itinerary updating.
2. Inline HOTEL SUGGESTIONS: when the user asks about stays (or on demand), surface 2-3 hotel options from the curated catalog (demo-01-seed) with image, price, and an 'add to trip' action that inserts a stay item and re-checks budget.
3. Preserve budget-fit: after every edit re-run/re-display the per-category + per-day budget breakdown; flag over-budget.

ARCHITECTURE: itinerary edits go through the canonical itinerary schema + domain money math (integer minor units, INV-009/010); no supplier shapes outside the supply adapter. Any schema change needs a versioned migration note in the plan. FakeLLM path must be deterministic and demoable without an API key (keyless FakeLLM). 

ACCEPTANCE: sign in -> generate a draft -> in the chat, add an activity, remove one, and swap a hotel via the curated catalog; the itinerary and budget update correctly and the changes persist to the trip. Works keyless (FakeLLM). PRD refs: §9.1 (AI assists: draft, pricing, resale-match), Pillar 1.

title: AI recommends MULTIPLE itinerary options, not one fixed (A3)
body:
OPERATOR (verbatim): 'AO should also recommend multiple options to the user not just one fixed.' Today PlannerDraftSchema returns exactly one plan (submit_itinerary_draft 'call exactly once'); to compare, the user must re-run.

BUILD multi-option generation + compare/select:
1. On generate, produce 2-3 DISTINCT itinerary options for the same inputs (e.g. differentiated by theme/pace/spend: 'Budget-savvy', 'Balanced', 'Premium' or 'Culture-forward' vs 'Relaxed'). FakeLLM must deterministically yield distinct-but-plausible variants for the keyless demo.
2. A compare UI: option cards/tabs showing each option's headline, day count, total vs budget, and a highlight or two; user picks one to open in the builder (which then supports conversational editing from demo-03).
3. Each option is a full canonical itinerary (so any can be booked/listed/shared).

INVARIANTS: budget math integer minor units (INV-009/010); each option a valid canonical itinerary. Keyless FakeLLM deterministic. ACCEPTANCE: generate -> see 2-3 clearly-different options with budget comparison -> pick one -> it opens and is editable/bookable. PRD refs: §9.1 'draft itineraries' (plural), 'resale-match recommendations'.

title: Planner redesign — human labels not raw enums, destination as country/city select, draft as hero card (B12 + UI)
body:
Today the planner is a 9-field grid form that EXPOSES RAW ENUM STRINGS to the user (budgetMode dropdown shows 'hardCap'/'target'; pace shows 'balanced'; destination is a bare text input placeholder 'e.g. Lisbon'). It reads as a debug form, not a product.

2. DESTINATION as a country/city selector (B12 'country selection'): a searchable picker seeded at least with the hero cities/countries (Portugal/Lisbon, Japan/Tokyo, Morocco/Marrakech, Iceland/Reykjavik) with flags/thumbnails; free-text still allowed as fallback.

UI BAR: match landing-page polish; premium, image-forward. ACCEPTANCE: the planner has zero raw enum strings, destination is a real selector, and the draft renders as a premium hero card. No change to the underlying draft/budget contract beyond presentation. PRD refs: §9.1 inputs (destination, dates, party, style/pace, budget).

title: Restyle sign-in / sign-up with the design system (kill inline styles) — first screen after landing must not look broken
body: Both auth forms (sign-in-form.tsx, sign-up-form.tsx) bypass the design system entirely with inline style={{}} and look unstyled next to the premium landing page — the first screen after landing reads as broken. title: Surface verified-seller badge + ratings prominently in marketplace (C17) — make the trust story visible
body: Verified sellers exist as an INVISIBLE gate (agencyVetting.isVetted enforced at list/license time) but there is NO trust badge shown anywhere in browse — the 'trust/verified sellers' story has nothing to point at. title: Discover / 'What's Hot' feed — country selection -> trending inspiration -> 'Plan this' seeds the builder (B6/B10)
body:
OPERATOR must-have: "What's new/hot in a country ... Discover / 'What's Hot' inspiration feed ... country selection." No discover/explore surface exists today (specs/006 explicitly excluded it). BUILD a top-of-funnel Discover page (new nav destination):
1. Country/destination selection (reuse the hero cities + countries), then a scrollable inspiration feed of trending places/experiences for that destination — image-forward cards (licensed imagery from demo-01 catalog / Unsplash source URLs; INV-025 licensed-only, no scraped/fabricated), a 'what's happening' blurb, and hotel highlights (B10 discovery-side hotel recommendations).

3. Seeded content is fine for the demo (no live events-API integration required) but must be labeled/real, not fabricated.

title: Self-drive vs 'request an agent to arrange' fork on the client-facing trip (A4)
body:
OPERATOR must-have: 'Clients should be able to request agents to host/arrange their itinerary for them if not available.' PRD §9.5 fork: self-drive (traveler books the assembled cart) vs request-agent (hand the plan to a marketplace agent who refines/executes; platform earns take-rate) — this keeps the consumer surface feeding the B2B marketplace. Nothing like it exists today (no consumer surface / handoff).

BUILD a lightweight fork on the client-facing trip view (/view/[token]): two clear paths — 'Book it myself' (self-drive, links into the existing booking flow / or a request-quote) and 'Have an agent arrange this for me' (request-agent). The request-agent path captures the client's contact + notes and creates a handoff/request record visible to the agent (a simple agent-side 'Trip requests' inbox with status: new/accepted). Keep it demo-simple (no full consumer auth): the value is showing the fork + the agent receiving the request. 

INVARIANTS: tenant scoping (INV-004) — requests route to the owning agency; provenance/client-ownership respected. ACCEPTANCE: on a shared client trip, the client can choose self-drive or request-an-agent; a request appears in the agent's inbox. PRD refs: §9.5 agent-vs-self-drive fork, Pillar 4.

title: Flight suggestions + deep-link handoff (display only — NOT merchant-of-record) (B13)
body: OPERATOR lists 'Flights' among must-haves. PRD is explicit (Non-goals + §9.3 bookable map + Risks): DO NOT be merchant-of-record for flights early; MVP = DEEP-LINK. So build DISPLAY + DEEP-LINK only, never in-platform flight booking/payment. BUILD a flights card in the builder/booking context: given the trip's origin/destination/dates, show 2-3 indicative flight options (seeded/sandbox: airline, times, indicative price as budget anchor) with a 'Search flights' / 'Book on partner' DEEP-LINK button that hands off (opens an external/partner URL). Make clear it is a deep-link, not an in-platform booking. Do NOT add flight items to the canonical bookable cart or create a flights merchant/payment path (respects the constitution / non-goal). Flights remain the budget anchor (domain/budget.ts) only. ACCEPTANCE: a flights card shows indicative options + a deep-link handoff; no flight is booked in-platform; no merchant-of-record path added. PRD refs: §9.3 (Flights = deep-link), Non-goals, Risks 'flights ops & thin margin'.

title: Group travel — agent posts a group departure (seats/capacity), travelers join, and it can be white-labeled (B2B2C + B2B2B)
body:
OPERATOR must-have (2026-07-13): 'include group travels as well ... basically agent posting for it. and it can be white-label as well.' A distinct marketplace/trade product on top of the existing single-itinerary marketplace.

BUILD group-departure trips:
1. AGENT POSTS a group trip: an itinerary + group metadata — departure date(s), total capacity (seats), per-seat price (integer minor units), and derived seats-remaining. Reuse the canonical itinerary + existing listing machinery; add group metadata rather than deep-forking the canonical schema. title: e2e: fullyParallel + real Better Auth rate limiting intermittently fails unrelated sign-up journeys
body:
Bug-sized -- infra/flake, not a product defect. Found live during demo-09-request-agent (spec 022) Live Test & Fix: a full `npx playwright test` run (default fullyParallel: true, playwright.config.ts, retries: 0 locally) failed 4 unrelated tests -- marketplace-journey.spec.ts, planner-journey.spec.ts, sign-in.spec.ts, and dashboard-shell-journey.spec.ts -- all at `signUpAgency`'s terminal `expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/dashboard$/)` assertion (support.ts:46), landing on /sign-up instead after exhausting its existing 3-attempt/11s-wait retry loop. Re-running the IDENTICAL suite with `--workers=2` passed all 34 tests, including the new trip-handoffs-journey.spec.ts (which itself performs 2 sign-ups) -- confirming the failures are real-provider rate-limiting under contention from too many concurrent sign-up requests sharing the compose stack's one client IP, not a regression from this ticket's change (support.ts's own comments already document this exact class from a prior iteration).

ROOT CAUSE: `playwright.config.ts` sets `fullyParallel: true` with no worker cap, so every spec file's sign-up runs in its own worker simultaneously; Better Auth's real per-endpoint rate limiter (intentionally not mocked, per architecture) has a fixed budget shared by the single container IP. As the suite grows (each new feature typically adds 1-2 more `signUpAgency` calls), the probability of tripping the limiter within the existing retry window rises -- this is likely to recur and worsen on every future ticket that adds an e2e spec with a sign-up.

FIX DIRECTION (test-infra, not touched by this ticket per the 'do not modify test infrastructure unless the ticket is about test infra' guardrail): either cap `workers` in playwright.config.ts to a small fixed number for local/loop runs (trades wall-clock time for reliability), or extend support.ts's existing retry budget (more attempts / longer backoff), or serialize sign-up-heavy specs via `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` suite-wide. Whichever direction is chosen must not weaken any assertion (the retry-and-still-fail behavior should stay a real failure, not silently swallowed).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
  1. A full `npx playwright test` run at the suite's current (or larger) size passes reliably across repeated runs at the DEFAULT worker/parallelism settings (no manual --workers override needed).
  2. No existing assertion is weakened; retries stay bounded and visible if a genuine failure occurs.

Evidence: this run's default-parallelism failure output + the immediate --workers=2 clean pass (34/34), both captured in demo-09-request-agent's PR discussion.

PRIORITY SCORE: Severity 1 (test-infra flake, not a product defect; CI does not run e2e today -- see OPERATOR-DESK CI-IMG-BUILD -- so this only affects loop-internal Live Test runs) + Frequency 2 (recurs on any run near/at current suite size, worsens as more sign-up-using specs are added) + Fix effort 3 (config/retry-budget change, no product code) = 6/9 -> low.

1. Client account area (consumer route group) listing the client's travels (itineraries shared to/with them, group trips joined) and their bookings (booking history with status + client-facing totals).
2. Association model linking client identity <-> itinerary/booking (see design question above); backfill/attach on share, join, or handoff-accept.
3. Each trip opens the existing white-labeled client-view (spec 010) — reuse, do not fork.

HALTS (DIRECTIVE / constitution — operator gates):
- SCHEMA: the client<->trip/booking linkage is a data-model/canonical-schema change -> versioned migration note + operator gate. No silent schema change.
- TRUST/INV-020: the client history shows ONLY client-facing prices/totals — NEVER markup, net-rate, or agency internals. Client identity scoping: a client sees ONLY their own trips/bookings, never another client's or any agency's data (identity + INV-004 tenant scoping).
- PROVENANCE: honest origin (Constitution VI).

TESTS: L3 that (a) a signed-in client sees exactly their own trips + bookings and nothing else, (b) no markup/net-rate leaks into any client history payload, (c) anonymous token client-view access still works unchanged (INV-018).

ACCEPTANCE: a signed-in client sees a 'My Trips' area with their travel history and booking history (client-facing figures only), each opening the branded client-view; associations are created when a trip is shared/joined/handed-off; strict client-scoping; no INV-020 leakage; schema migration + Constitution P2 note present; schema landed via operator gate.

Feature-sized -> route through Spec Kit. Depends on: p2-consumer-accounts-identity; spec 010 (client-view), seed-0005/0026 (bookings), spec 021 (group travel), spec 022 (handoffs).
